items.stem: Complete the statement: A statement of affairs is …
options: a statement of assets and liabilities used to calculate capital when records are incomplete
an income statement for a club
items.answer: a statement of assets and liabilities used to calculate capital when records are incomplete
items.markingKey: a statement of assets and liabilities used to calculate capital when records are incomplete. Capital = assets − liabilities [1]

items.stem: Explain why drawings are added to the change in capital when calculating profit.
items.answer: Drawings reduced closing capital but were taken out of profit; adding them back gives the profit actually earned.
items.markingKey: Drawings reduced capital [1]; added back to find profit earned [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two disadvantages to a sole trader of not keeping full double-entry records.
items.answer: Profit cannot be analysed by source; errors and fraud are harder to detect; the bank or tax authorities may not accept the figures; control of receivables and payables is difficult.

items.answer: Credit sales are the missing figure: closing receivables + cash received + discounts allowed + irrecoverable debts − opening receivables.

items.stem: Explain why cash taken from the till before banking must be added back to find total sales.
items.answer: Payments made out of takings never reached the bank, so banked amounts understate the cash actually received from customers.

items.stem: Complete the statement: Goods costing $80 are sold for $100. The mark-up is …
Distinguish between mark-up and margin.
items.answer: Mark-up is gross profit as a percentage of cost; margin is gross profit as a percentage of selling price (revenue).
items.markingKey: Mark-up – on cost [1]; margin – on selling price [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how mark-up can be used to estimate the value of inventory lost in a fire.
items.answer: Using the normal mark-up, cost of sales is found from sales; cost of goods available less cost of sales gives the inventory that should have been held; less inventory saved = loss.
items.markingKey: COS from sales via mark-up [1]; expected inventory − saved = loss [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how missing drawings can be found.
items.answer: From the cash/bank account: all known receipts and payments are entered, and the balancing figure needed to reach the closing balance is taken to be drawings.

At 1 January the business had premises $95,000, equipment $19,900, inventory $7,700, trade receivables $2,700, bank $3,330, trade payables $2,600, loan $10,000. At 31 December it had premises $95,000, equipment $17,910, inventory $10,950, trade receivables $3,170, bank $1,760, trade payables $3,400, loan $8,000. During the year Leila took drawings of $10,100 and paid in additional capital of $3,900. (a) Calculate the capital at 1 January and at 31 December. (b) Advise Leila whether to start keeping full double-entry records.
items.answer: (a) Opening $116,030; closing $117,390 (b) Full records give detailed information, control and credibility with lenders, but cost time or bookkeeping fees; for a growing business the benefits usually outweigh the costs.

items.stem: Complete the statement: Takings are banked after paying wages of $200 a week in cash. To find total cash takings you must …
options: add the cash payments to the amounts banked
deduct the payments from the amounts banked
items.answer: add the cash payments to the amounts banked
items.markingKey: add the cash payments to the amounts banked. Cash used before banking [1]

items.stem: Nadia keeps only a cash book for Lagoon Boatworks. For the year: trade receivables were $8,610 at the start and $2,190 at the end; $62,520 was received from credit customers after allowing discounts of $1,040. Trade payables were $4,810 at the start and $7,650 at the end; $56,520 was paid to suppliers. A student calculated credit sales as $69,980. Identify the error and state the correct credit sales.
items.answer: The opening and closing receivables were used the wrong way round: closing receivables are added and opening receivables deducted. Correct credit sales: $57,140.
items.markingKey: Error: the opening and closing receivables were used the wrong way round: closing receivables are added and opening receivables deducted [1]; correct credit sales: $57,140 [1] [2]

Kilimanjaro Coffee sells goods at a mark-up of 33⅓% on cost. Revenue for the year was $48,000; inventory was $4,700 at the start and $5,200 at the end of the year. A trainee accountant calculated gross profit as $16,000. Identify the error and state the correct gross profit.
items.answer: The mark-up (a percentage of cost) was applied to revenue; revenue must be multiplied by the margin. Correct gross profit: $12,000.

items.stem: A fire destroyed most of the inventory of Jade Ceramics on 30 April. Inventory at 1 January was $14,500; purchases from 1 January to 30 April were $63,900; sales for the same period were $81,600. Jade Ceramics sells all goods at a mark-up of 20%. Inventory costing $2,300 was saved. An accounts assistant calculated cost of sales as $65,280. Explain the error and calculate the correct cost of sales, showing your working.
items.answer: The mark-up percentage was applied to selling price as if it were a margin. Correct cost of sales: $68,000.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the mark-up percentage was applied to selling price as if it were a margin [1]; working: $81,600 × 100/120 [1]; correct cost of sales: $68,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Nile Valley Dairy sells goods at a mark-up of 20% on cost. Revenue for the year was $78,000; inventory was $14,400 at the start and $9,800 at the end of the year. Calculate the gross profit and the cost of sales.
items.answer: Gross profit $13,000; cost of sales $65,000

items.stem: Yusuf owns Jade Ceramics and keeps limited records. Receipts from customers $119,920; payments to suppliers $66,080; general expenses paid $14,580. Opening and closing balances: trade receivables $5,880 and $2,690; trade payables $4,360 and $5,080; inventory $8,000 and $5,900; general expenses owing $360 and $410. All sales and purchases are on credit. A junior clerk calculated profit for the year as $33,250. Identify the error and state the correct profit.
items.answer: Expenses paid were used without adjusting for the opening and closing accruals. Correct profit: $33,200.
items.markingKey: Error: expenses paid were used without adjusting for the opening and closing accruals [1]; correct profit: $33,200 [1] [2]
